channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Kazakhstan Updates Car Recycling Program to Combat Corruption and Middlemen
item.description: Kazakhstan's "Zhassyl Damu" is revising its old car recycling program to eliminate corruption and middlemen. The company is negotiating with recyclers and aims to ensure direct benefits for vehicle owners. Past issues with a sole contractor led to investigations and convictions.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee Finds Consumer Rights Violations in 132 Construction Contracts
item.description: Uzbekistan's Competition Committee has identified restrictive consumer rights clauses in contracts from 132 construction organizations. Over 1700 complaints were received regarding construction quality and delays. The committee ensured the recalculation of nearly 14.5 billion soums in favor of consumers.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Reform Auto Insurance: Repair Option and New Tariffs Introduced
item.description: Kazakhstan is preparing a major reform of auto insurance. If the bill passes, drivers will be able to choose between monetary compensation and car repair by the insurance company after an accident. The insurer will inspect the car and issue a repair order, with work to be completed within 30 working days.

item.title: Over 700 Labor Rights Restored in Kazakhstan's Zhetysu Region
item.description: The prosecutor's office in Kazakhstan's Zhetysu region has restored the labor rights of over 700 citizens. Violations included missing accident insurance contracts for 70 workers and failure to provide social leave. Additionally, 25 employers were fined, and over 50 unemployed individuals were placed in jobs.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Qazaq Bitum Processing Raises 5 Billion Tenge on Stock Exchange
item.description: Qazaq Bitum Processing, a major bitumen producer in Kazakhstan, successfully raised 5 billion tenge through a bond offering on the KASE stock exchange. The initial target was 1 billion tenge, but demand reached 11.1 billion tenge, leading to an increased placement. Private investors acquired 66% of the issue.

item.title: Uzbek President Addresses SCO-Plus Experts on Security Issues in Samarkand
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev addressed participants of the first SCO-Plus expert dialogue on security issues in Samarkand. He noted the dialogue aims to discuss pressing threats and risks, and to define practical cooperation for ensuring security and sustainable development.

item.title: Cyber Domain Becomes Main Arena for Confrontations, Says Uzbek President
item.description: Uzbek President Shavkat Mirziyoyev stated that the cyber domain has become a primary arena for confrontations, alongside traditional methods. He highlighted the increasing use of network attacks, manipulation of public opinion, and dissemination of disinformation, posing new vulnerabilities.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Business Ombudsman: A Reliable Protector of Entrepreneurs' Rights
item.description: The Business Ombudsman in Uzbekistan plays a crucial role in safeguarding entrepreneurs from unlawful state interference. Over 10,740 appeals were received in nine months, with nearly 48% resulting in restored rights. The office has become an effective mechanism for protecting business interests, annulling unjustified decisions, and removing bureaucratic barriers.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extends Mortgage Concessions for Three More Years
item.description: Kazakhstan has extended preferential mortgage terms for three years until December 31, 2029. Borrowers through the housing construction savings system will no longer be subject to the mandatory debt-to-income ratio requirement. This allows individuals whose monthly loan payments exceed 50% of their income to still obtain a mortgage.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Platform for Collective Debt Settlement
item.description: Kazakhstan has launched Finkelisim.kz, a platform developed by the Financial Market Development Agency and the First Credit Bureau. It allows citizens with multiple loans from various institutions to apply for collective debt settlement through mediation. The platform aims to help borrowers negotiate a unified payment schedule with creditors.

item.title: Kazakhstan Police Suspend Brother of Ex-Speaker's Raider Case
item.description: Police in Kazakhstan's Karaganda region have suspended a high-profile criminal case involving alleged raiding. The case accused Yerlan Nigmatulin, brother of former parliament speaker Nurlan Nigmatulin, of forcing businessman Ramis Ibrahimov to transfer his transport business in 2016. The investigation was halted due to an 'unidentified person'.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extends Ban on Gasoline and Diesel Exports for Six Months
item.description: Kazakhstan has extended its ban on the export of gasoline, diesel fuel, and other petroleum products for another six months, from November 22, 2026, to May 22, 2027. The Energy Ministry signed the order, which also prohibits the export of light distillates and other oil products outside the EAEU from January 1 to June 30, 2027.

item.title: Uzbekistan Aims to Boost Meat Production Amid Rising Demand
item.description: Uzbekistan's domestic meat production is struggling to meet growing demand due to population and consumption increases. The Minister of Agriculture cited underdeveloped fodder bases and infrastructure as key reasons. New measures include establishing livestock complexes near cotton and grain fields, with plans to build 16,000 such complexes this year to significantly increase meat output.

item.title: Teenager Sentenced to 15 Years for Attempted Murder of Schoolgirl in Atyrau
item.description: A teenager in Atyrau has been sentenced to 15 years in prison for the attempted murder of a 13-year-old schoolgirl. The ninth-grader attacked the eighth-grader five times with a knife in a school corridor. The court considered surveillance footage and the teenager's phone and notebook entries, which indicated intentions of revenge. He will serve his sentence in a juvenile facility.

item.title: Average Speed Control to Be Launched on Several Kazakhstan Highways
item.description: Average speed control systems will be implemented on several republican highways in Kazakhstan starting November 9, 2026. These systems monitor speed over entire zones, not just at camera points, to enhance road safety.

item.title: Uzbekistan Proposes Opening UN Counter-Terrorism Regional Office
item.description: Uzbekistan's President Shavkat Mirziyoyev has proposed opening a regional office of the UN Counter-Terrorism Directorate in the country. This office would provide practical assistance to Central Asian states in combating terrorism, including leveraging artificial intelligence.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Detains Suspects with 63 Kilograms of Hashish
item.description: Kyrgyz authorities have seized 63 kilograms of hashish of Afghan origin in the Osh region, disrupting an international drug trafficking channel. Three individuals were detained for allegedly smuggling the drugs from Tajikistan through Kyrgyzstan to Kazakhstan and Russia.

item.title: Kazakhstan Tests Hospital Directors; One in Five Fails Qualification Exam
item.description: Kazakhstan has begun assessing the qualifications of heads of maternity wards, children's hospitals, and emergency services. In the initial phase, 47 out of 235 tested managers, including 25 chief physicians and 22 deputies, failed to achieve the required score. The Ministry of Health stated that professional competence directly impacts healthcare quality and patient safety.

item.title: US Congressman Expresses Concern Over RFE/RL Journalist Accreditation Issues in Kazakhstan
item.description: US Congressman Robert Aderholt has voiced concern over Kazakhstan's delays in accrediting journalists from Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty (RFE/RL). He urged Kazakh authorities to allow RFE/RL correspondents to work freely, emphasizing the importance of US influence in Central Asia and countering China's role in the strategically vital region.

item.title: Kazakhstan May Restrict Single-Use Plastics Following International Treaty
item.description: Kazakhstan is participating in UN discussions for an international treaty that will impose strict limitations on plastic use, including single-use items, except in medical fields. The Vice Minister of Ecology and Natural Resources stated that once adopted, the treaty will significantly restrict or eliminate single-use plastics within Kazakhstan, as most countries aim to reduce plastic pollution.

item.title: President's Address Working Group Visits North Kazakhstan Region
item.description: A working group tasked with explaining President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev's address visited the North Kazakhstan region. Discussions focused on implementing presidential initiatives, developing social infrastructure, improving living standards, and addressing regional issues. Key priorities include transport infrastructure development, healthcare modernization, agricultural support, and enhancing citizen well-being.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Explains Inability to Stricter Penalize Kaztsink for Air Pollution
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Ecology and Natural Resources explained why stricter penalties cannot be imposed on Kaztsink for regular air pollution violations. While the company faces administrative fines, existing legislation lacks provisions for more severe sanctions against a single legal entity. The ministry noted that companies are required to reduce emissions during unfavorable meteorological conditions.

item.title: Turkmenistan Imports Block Meat and Live Cattle to Address Meat Shortage
item.description: Turkmenistan is importing block meat and live cattle to alleviate a growing meat deficit. New, cheaper meat, including buffalo meat, is appearing in state stores and markets in Ashgabat and Kipchak. This follows months of rising prices and public discontent, with some citizens detained for protesting high costs.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Proposes AI and Digital ID for Driver's Licenses and Vehicle Registration
item.description: Kyrgyzstan is considering changes to vehicle registration and driver's license procedures, including AI for exam control and digital identification via the 'Tunduk' app. Mopeds and light motorcycles will require registration. Drivers will be able to present documents electronically, and AI will monitor exams, with examiners wearing body cameras.

item.title: Kazakhstan Deputies Discuss Presidential Address Priorities and Regional Development
item.description: Members of the Kurultai met with residents in the East Kazakhstan region to discuss the priorities of the President's Address and socio-economic development. Discussions covered economic growth, infrastructure modernization, and quality of life improvements. Significant investments are planned for social infrastructure, healthcare, and education facilities.

item.title: Kazakh Millionaire Eduard Ogai Establishes New Holding Company
item.description: Kazakh millionaire Eduard Ogai has launched a new holding company, Bala Urpek Limited, registered at the Astana International Financial Centre (AIFC). The company, capitalized at $1,000, will be headed by Nurakhmet Nuriev, former chairman of Kazakhmys. Ogai holds a significant stake in Kazakhmys Copper.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Reviews Sokuluk District's Development Progress
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov of Kyrgyzstan visited the Sokuluk district in the Chuy region to review its socio-economic development from 2021 to September 2026. The report highlighted the opening of 41 large enterprises, 189 SMEs, and significant job creation, alongside infrastructure improvements and new social facilities.

item.title: All Young Footballers Affected by Poisoning in Tashkent Returning to Kazakhstan
item.description: All participants of a football festival hospitalized in Tashkent with poisoning symptoms are returning to Kazakhstan. The Ministry of Health of Uzbekistan reported that their condition improved after medical care, and they have been discharged. Investigations into the cause of the mass poisoning are ongoing.

item.title: Lawyer Claims Kyrgyz Activist Tulemat Kurenov's Detention Period Exceeded
item.description: Lawyer Asel Argymbaeva stated that activist Tulemat Kurenov's detention period expired on October 10. She claims the court is violating the law by keeping him in pre-trial detention beyond the legal limit. Kurenov was detained on April 19, 2025, and his case arrived in court on October 10, 2025. The next hearing is November 10.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Vehicle Recycling Program Launch Delayed Due to Corruption Concerns
item.description: The launch of Kazakhstan's vehicle recycling program is delayed as authorities investigate past corruption schemes. A previous operator allegedly facilitated multiple submissions of the same vehicle with forged documents and allowed resellers to exploit the system. New mechanisms are being developed to ensure citizens directly benefit.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Establish Strategic Uranium Reserve, First Nuclear Power Plant Construction May Begin in 2027
item.description: Kazakhstan plans to create a strategic uranium reserve to ensure future nuclear power plants have sufficient domestic resources. Despite being a leading uranium producer, much of the extracted material is exported. The country aims to reserve 100,000 tons by 2040 and 150,000 tons by 2050. Construction of the first NPP could start in 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Launch Waste-to-Energy Plants by 2028 with Chinese Investment
item.description: Kazakhstan will introduce waste-to-energy facilities, with three plants to be built in Astana, Almaty, and Shymkent by 2028 through a $650 million investment from Chinese companies. These facilities aim to reduce landfill waste and generate electricity and heat. Similar projects are being considered for other regions.

item.title: Iran Claims Two Tankers Hit Mines in Strait of Hormuz, Causing Fires
item.description: Iran's Revolutionary Guard reported two oil tankers struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz, leading to fires. They claim the vessels were violating navigation rules and attempting to use unauthorized routes, allegedly with US military support. Iran insists the strait's conditions will not change until its demands are met.

item.title: Ishak Masaliev Submits Candidacy for Kyrgyzstan Presidential Election
item.description: Ishak Masaliev has officially submitted his application to the Central Election Commission to run for President of Kyrgyzstan. The former Member of Parliament becomes the fifth contender to register for the upcoming election. The deadline for candidate nominations is November 13.

item.title: US Court Temporarily Halts Deportation of Afghan Nationals Amid Safety Concerns
item.description: A federal judge in New York has temporarily halted the planned deportation of dozens of Afghan nationals. The decision came after lawmakers and rights groups warned that sending them back to Afghanistan or Pakistan could endanger their lives. The order is in effect until November 7.

item.title: Uzbekistan's Annual Inflation Accelerates to 6.5% in October
item.description: Uzbekistan's consumer prices rose by 0.6% in October, leading to an annual inflation rate of 6.5%, up from 6.4% in September. Food prices increased by 1% monthly and 6.4% annually. Non-food items saw a 0.2% monthly rise and 5.6% annually, while services increased by 0.6% monthly and 7.3% annually.

item.title: Kara-Jantak Village Residents Transferred to Kyrgyzstan Receive Housing Documents
item.description: Residents of Kara-Jantak village, which transferred from Uzbekistan to Kyrgyzstan following border delimitation, have received state certificates for their residences. A total of 295 properties were processed. Passports confirming Kyrgyz citizenship were previously issued to the villagers.

item.title: All Kazakh Junior Footballers Hospitalized After Food Poisoning in Tashkent Discharged
item.description: All junior athletes from Kazakhstan hospitalized in Tashkent due to food poisoning have been discharged after their condition improved, reported the Uzbek Ministry of Health. The young footballers, who fell ill on October 31 after breakfast, have returned to their homeland. The ministry stated that medical decisions for discharge were made after all affected individuals showed improvement.

item.title: Uzbekistan Focuses on Tourism Development with Visa Liberalization and Specialized Training
item.description: Uzbekistan is prioritizing its tourism industry as a strategic economic sector, implementing long-term state initiatives. These include visa cancellations, promoting safe tourism, and developing diverse tourism types from gastronomic to eco-tourism. The nation aims to enhance its appeal through unique natural sites and rich cultural heritage, while also focusing on training qualified tourism professionals.

item.title: Karakalpak activist reports improved prison conditions after UN appeal
item.description: Karakalpak activist Dauletmurat Tajimuratov, imprisoned in Uzbekistan, has reported improved conditions in Colony No. 17 following an appeal to the UN. A commission led by the ombudsman visited the facility, and Tajimuratov noted a reduction in mistreatment, including an end to beatings.
